title: Mirror label
statement:
A label printer checks whether a label reads the same forwards and backwards. It looks only at letters and digits, ignores case, and skips spaces and punctuation.

Return true if `label` reads the same in both directions under those rules.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Which characters count?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Only letters and digits. Ignore spaces and punctuation.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Is an empty label, or one with only punctuation, a mirror?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes, there is nothing to contradict it.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Can I build a cleaned copy, or should I use constant extra space?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Either works; constant space is the follow-up.

approaches.name: Clean and reverse
approaches.idea: Build a string of the lowercase letters and digits and compare it with its reverse.
approaches.tradeoffs: Very readable but uses a copy of the string.

approaches.name: Two pointers
approaches.idea: Move one pointer from each end, skipping characters that are not letters or digits, and compare the lowercase characters.
approaches.tradeoffs: No copy; slightly more care with the skipping logic.

optimal.name: Two pointers from both ends
optimal.explanation: Start i at 0 and j at the end. While i < j: skip a non-alphanumeric character on either side, otherwise compare lowercase characters and fail on a mismatch, then move both inward. Return true when the pointers meet.

What if one pointer starts at each end?
Move two pointers inward, skipping characters that are not letters or digits, comparing lowercase characters.

followUps: Allow at most one character to be removed to make a mirror.
The label is Unicode text. What changes about "letters and digits"?

walkthrough.say: I only compare letters and digits, case-insensitive, right? And an empty label or one that’s all punctuation counts as a mirror?
The quickest version is to filter to lowercase letters and digits, then compare with the reverse. That’s O(n) time but O(n) extra space for the copy.
I can avoid the copy with two pointers, one at each end, skipping anything that isn’t a letter or digit. Still O(n) time, now O(1) space.
Each loop step does exactly one thing: skip on the left, skip on the right, or compare and move both.
If both sides are real characters, compare them ignoring case.
Step on no pets: S and s match, t and t, e and e, then the space is skipped, p and p, and so on to the middle. True.
Route 66: R against 6 fails immediately, so false. And for one a two, 1 against 2 fails, which checks that digits aren’t skipped.
